newsitem.title: USA: Santa Anita recapitalization offer made.
newsitem.headline: Santa Anita recapitalization offer made.

text.p: Apollo Real Estate Advisors and The Koll Co said Wednesday it made a $27 per paired share cash proposal to Santa Anita Realty Enterprises Inc and Santa Anita Operating Co's board to recapitalize the companies.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the investors said the companies would pay a special cash dividend of $11 per paired share to all current shareholders.

In the recapitalization, the companies would commence a self-tender offer to buy up to 5.6 million paired shares in which current stockholders of the companies would have a number of options in addition to the payment of $11 special dividend.

Those options include retaining their existing paired shares, receive $16 in cash per paired share or receive per paired share an additional $11 in cash together with one warrant to buy one paired share at $16.25 per paired shares for a five-year period.
The two companies are traded on the New York Stock Exchange as paired shares.

Apollo and Koll hold 989,900 paired shares of the Santa Anita companies, purchased for $19.9 million. The shares represent a stake of 8.6 percent in Santa Anita Realty and 8.7 percent in Santa Anita Operating, the filing showed.
The latest transactions include the purchase of 18,500 paired shares between November 11, 1996 and November 21, 1996 at prices ranging from $24.50 to $25.3875 per paired share.m

Koll Arcadia Investors LLC said it believes its transaction allows stockholders of the companies to monetize their present gains in the paired shares without causing significant market impact, the filing said.

Koll Arcadia also entered into a letter agreement with Gotham Partners, another investor in the Santa Anita companies, on January 28 in which Gotham would buy on a stand-by basis up to 5.6 million warrants from the companies at $5 per warrant.
In consideration for the stand-by agreement, Gotham would receive certain fees conditioned upon the number of paired shares purchased in the self-tender, the filing said.

According the letter agreement, Gotham would buy from companies one warrant for each paired share bought by the companies relating to the terms of the self-tender $16 all cash election, the filing said.
